Shew
shō
v. (the Authorized Version's spelling of show; rendering Hebrew ra'ah in the causative and 'asah, Greek deiknumi)
An older spelling of show, pronounced the same, from Saxon sceawian, to look at or display. The Authorized Version spells it shew throughout, which is why the table in the tabernacle is the table of shewbread — the bread of the presence, set out where God could see it.

Biblical Definition

Shew is the Authorized Version's spelling of show, and it covers both what God displays and what men are commanded to display. God's call to Abram is built on it, and on a deliberate withholding: “Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee” (Genesis 12:1). The land is not named. Abram must leave everything before he learns where he is going, and Hebrews notes that he went out not knowing whither he went. The psalmist asks for the same kind of showing in the moral realm: “Shew me thy ways, O LORD; teach me thy paths” (Psalm 25:4). The prophets turn the verb toward conduct: “Execute true judgment, and shew mercy and compassions every man to his brother” (Zechariah 7:9), and Isaiah's bracing summons, “Remember this, and shew yourselves men” (Isaiah 46:8). And Christ promises that the Spirit will shew His disciples what belongs to Him: “he shall take of mine, and shall shew it unto you” (John 16:15).

Webster 1828 Definition

The Authorized Version's spelling of show: to display, to make known, to point out. In Scripture it is used of the land God would shew Abram, the ways the psalmist asks to be shewn, and the mercy men are commanded to shew one another.

expand to see more

SHEW, v.t. [Sax. sceawian, to look at.] To exhibit or present to view; to display. The older spelling of show.

2. To make known; to reveal; to teach; as, shew me thy ways.

3. To bestow; to confer; as, to shew mercy, to shew kindness.

4. SHEWBREAD, n. The bread set every sabbath before the Lord on the table in the sanctuary.

5. In Scripture, unto a land that I will shew thee, Gen. 12; shew mercy and compassions every man to his brother, Zech. 7.

Key Scripture

Genesis 12:1 — "Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee:"

Psalm 25:4 — "Shew me thy ways, O LORD; teach me thy paths."

Zechariah 7:9 — "Thus speaketh the LORD of hosts, saying, Execute true judgment, and shew mercy and compassions every man to his brother:"

Isaiah 46:8 — "Remember this, and shew yourselves men: bring it again to mind, O ye transgressors."

Modern Corruption

Guidance is now widely sought as advance information — a map of the future disclosed before obedience begins. God's dealing with Abram runs the other way: the going comes first, and the shewing follows.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle needing recovery is that God's revealed will is for obedience and His secret will is not ours to inspect. Abram is told to leave and is not told where he will arrive; the land is a land that I will shew thee, future tense, and Hebrews commends him precisely for going out not knowing. Deuteronomy 29:29 draws the line: the secret things belong unto the LORD our God, but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children, that we may do all the words of this law.

A great deal of Christian anxiety about guidance is the attempt to cross that line — to obtain, before acting, the information God has reserved. Psalm 25:4 shows the prayer Scripture actually models: Shew me thy ways, O LORD; teach me thy paths, a request for the character of God's ways rather than a preview of events. The believer is furnished for every decision by the commandments, by wisdom, and by counsel, and is not promised more. What remains hidden is not withheld unkindly; it is the difference between a creature and his Maker, and accepting it is most of what trust means.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew ra'ah in the causative stem means to cause to see, to shew; 'asah chesed is to do or shew mercy. Greek deiknumi is to point out or exhibit, and anadeiknumi to display openly.

expand to see more

Hebrew ra'ah (H7200) — to see; in the causative stem, to cause to see, to shew.

Hebrew chesed (H2617) — covenant mercy, lovingkindness; what men are commanded to shew one another in Zechariah 7:9.

Hebrew lechem happanim (H3899, H6440) — the bread of the faces or of the presence; the shewbread of the sanctuary.

Greek deiknumi (G1166) — to shew, point out, exhibit; used of the Spirit shewing the things of Christ.

Saxon sceawian — to look at, to behold; the root of both shew and show.

Usage

"Of a call obeyed before the destination is known: unto a land that I will shew thee (Genesis 12:1)."

"Of prayer for the character of God's ways: Shew me thy ways, O LORD; teach me thy paths (Psalm 25:4)."

"Of mercy required between brethren: shew mercy and compassions every man to his brother (Zechariah 7:9)."
